lore_items.name: Knotted Cord
lore_items.description: A hand's length of cord with knots tied down it at uneven spacing, each pulled tight and sealed with a dab of wax. It has been carried against skin for a long time.

lore_items.name: Ronin's Day Tally
lore_items.description: A flat strip of hide scored with short cuts in rows of ten. The last rows are fresh. The first are so old they have gone smooth.

lore_items.name: Scraped Hide Strip
lore_items.description: A strip of cured hide, the edge frayed from a belt. A mark was burned into it and someone has tried to scrape the mark away, and failed.

lore_items.name: Folded Page
lore_items.description: A single page folded into quarters and unfolded so often it has split along the creases. The writing is in a hand nobody near here uses, and the last line is lost to a tear.

lore_items.name: Dented Coin
lore_items.description: A coin of the old kind, bent double and straightened again. Someone has scratched a line across the face, and not in anger.

lore_items.name: Sealed Note
lore_items.description: A note folded small and sealed with a thumb of tallow. Nothing is written on the outside. The inside is not for you.

say: Stranger. I have a cord, and every knot in it's a name. I can't give it to anyone here and I can't burn it. Will you take it past the walls?
You travel and I don't. There are people outside who work against the slavers. A knotted cord for them. Nobody here must see you take it.
Keep your voice low. I have something small and it has to leave the Nation. Not for coin.
Would you carry a thing for me? It weighs nothing. If a priest found it on me it would weigh a great deal.
I asked three men and was refused by three. I will ask you. A knotted cord, to anyone who works against the slavers. That is all of it.
accept: Who do I give it to?
accepted: Here. Anyone who stands against the slavers. Say it is from inside and do not say whose hand. Then come back and tell me it was taken.
Tuck it away. Past the gates, find one who frees slaves and put it in their hand. They will understand it. Come back and say they did.
Do not look at it here. It is only a cord. Give it to the slaver-breakers beyond the walls, and return when it is done.
Thank you. Do not thank me back. Carry it to the ones who free slaves, and tell me it reached them.
decline: That is a risk I will not take.

say: That's a lot of knots for a bit of string. Who tied them?
Cord, knotted, carried a long way by the look of it. Where from?
You have something in your hand you keep not looking at.
Hold up. A knotted cord. Someone wanted that gone from wherever it was. Where from?
reply: From inside the Holy Nation. A woman who gave no name.
A woman behind the walls. She wants it to reach you.
Out of the Nation, from someone who counts names.
I was asked to bring it to whoever frees slaves.
after: Then she is still counting. Tell her it came to hands that will not drop it.
A name for every knot, I would guess. Tell her it was taken, and not laughed at.
I have spent a long time wishing I knew what was behind those walls. This is a start. Say so.
Brave, and a fool, and I owe her for both. Tell her we have it.

say: They took it? Then it is out of my hands. Here, this coat was put aside for something else. I would rather you had it, and some coin.
It reached someone. Thank you. I will not ask who. Take this coat and these cats, and I will not forget the rest.
Taken, and not turned in. You do not know what that is worth. Take the coat and the cats, and please do not come to me again.
Then it left. Good. That is all I wanted from it. Take this coat, the cats, and a favour owed.
I thought you would be seen, or sell it. You did neither. Here's what I can spare, and a coat I mended myself.
Stranger. I keep count of days. It's all I keep. Take the count to the hive. They'll know what it is.
I lost the hive. I didn't lose the days. I cut them, one by one. Someone should hold them. Will you carry them to the hive?
The hive is quiet for me now. Not for them. Would you take something to them, so they know I'm still marking?
No one asks me for anything. I have a thing to give. It's a count. It's small. It must go to the hive.
A strip of hide. Cuts in it. I can't walk into the hive anymore.
accept: Whom do I give it to?
accepted: Here. Any of the hive. They will understand rows of cuts. Say it is from one outside. Then come back and say it was held.
Take it. It is light. Put it in the hands of one of them, and say who sent it. Then tell me what they did.
Keep it dry. Give it to the hive when you meet them. They do not need me to explain. Come back and tell me.
Here. It is everything I have counted. Do not lose it. Bring me word after.

say: That is a lot of small cuts. Someone made them for a long time. Who?
You carry marks. Marks of days. I know the shape of them. Whose?
That isn't ours. It's of ours. What's it?
Cuts in rows. One for each. There are many. Where did it come from?
reply: A ronin outside the hive. He counts the days and wanted you to know.
From one who left, or was left. He keeps this count.
A hive prince alone out there asked me to bring it.
From a lone ronin. He wants the hive to hold it.
after: He counts. Alone. We did not know. The hive will hold it. Say to him: held.
We will keep it. Nobody told us someone still counted. Tell him so.
One cut for each day he has been out. That is a lot of days. Tell him we have them.
Held. We have no mark for what he is. But we have this. Tell him.

say: Held. I didn't expect them to say it. Take these. And a favour, if I can ever give you one.
They kept it. Good. I think I'd like to sit a while. Take these, they aren't enough.
Held. That word. It's more than I had yesterday. Take what I can give.
You carried it and they took it. I am glad. Take this, and know I am in your debt.
They have the days now. I only have what comes next.
/FLATSKIN/. I have a thing the Kingdom should have back. I can't carry it there. You can.
I won't beg. I ask once. Take this to a Shek in the Kingdom. Say nothing of where you had it.
There's something I owe and can't pay. It must be put in a Shek hand, in the Kingdom. Will you?
My own people won't see me. They would see you. Take this hide to them.
A scrap of hide. It was mine. It belongs where I cannot go.
accepted: Here. A Shek of the Kingdom, any who will take it. Say nothing of me but that it is returned. Then come back.
Take it. A Shek who wears his horns, at a stall or at a gate. Put it in his hand. Come back and say he took it.
Do not look at it. Do not ask. Carry it to the Kingdom and put it in a Shek's hand. Then return.
It weighs nothing. Remember I said nothing of where I am. Bring me word after.

say: A mark on that hide has been scraped away. Not well enough. Where did you get it?
/FLATSKIN/. That's Shek leather. Who gave it to you, and why do you bring it here?
You carry something of ours. Don't hold it back.
That hide. I know what it is. I don't know how you came by it.
reply: A Shek outside the Kingdom asked me to return it. He did not say where he is.
From a Shek who cannot come himself. He asked that it go to a hand of the Kingdom.
I was given it to carry here. The one who gave it keeps his name to himself.
It was given to me for the Kingdom. By a Shek who is not here.
after: Hrm. Then he lives. Leave it with me. I did not speak with you.
Hrm. I know the hand that cut it. Tell him nothing. I heard nothing. But the Kingdom has it back.
Returned. That is something. A debt is a debt, outside or in. Go on, /FLATSKIN/.
Leave it on the counter. Go. If he asks, say it was taken without a word.

say: Taken, and nothing said. Good. Take these. A Shek pays what he owes, even from a long way off.
You put it in a Shek hand and lived. I've seen less from my own kin. Take this, /FLATSKIN/.
It's out of my keeping. That's enough. These cats aren't the debt.
Hrm. You did as I asked and didn't talk. Take this. I'll remember it.
Returned. I won't ask what was said. Take what I can spare.
I took a page off a dead man in the ruins. Old script, I can't read it. A skeleton can. Take it, tell me what it says.
You know skeletons? They read the old marks. I have a page I can't make out. Show it to one and bring me the sense.
I don't pay for what I don't understand. I have a page. Find a skeleton, have it read, tell me.
Dead man's page, ruins, old writing. Could be a map. Could be a shopping list. Have a skeleton read it.
accepted: Here. Any skeleton who will read. Ask what it says and nothing else. Skeletons talk plain. Come back.
Keep it flat. It is old and it will tear. A skeleton, then me. Bring the sense, not the paper.
Take it. Do not trade it, do not lose it. A skeleton can read it. I want the words.
Here. Ask, and then come back with what they say.

say: That page has been folded many times. The paper is failing. I can read what remains.
You're holding written material. I recognise the script.
That's an old page. I know the hand. Do you want me to read it?
You have a document. I haven't seen this form in some time.
reply: Read it to me. I was told you could.
Yes. What does it say?
A Tech Hunter found it. Tell me what it says.
Please. The sense, nothing more.
after: It is a list of names with a number beside each. The last number is unfinished. I will not guess what it counted. Tell the one who sent you.
It is a requisition for something never delivered. It was signed twice, in two hands. Tell the one who sent you that it is only that.
It is a note from someone who expected to be found. It asks that the finder not be afraid. Tell them.
It is a count of days with no conclusion. I have read it. I have no other comment. I will keep it.

say: You got it read. Good. I won't ask what it said, your face told me enough.
Read, and not worth much, from your look. Still, a job is a job. Here.
A skeleton read it? Did it ask for anything? No? Then it was honest. Cats, as agreed.
Done, then. I owe you the pay.
Good. The page has been on my mind. It will be off it now.
I have a coin that doesn't belong to me anymore. There are people who undo my trade. Take it to them.
Don't look at me like that. I owe the other side of this business, and I mean to pay it quietly. A coin, to the ones who cut shackles.
A man I sold was owed more than he got. I can't pay him. I can pay the ones who dig men out. Will you carry this?
Business teaches you what a debt is. This one has sat on me. A coin to the anti-slavers, or whatever they call themselves.
I deal in people and I know what I am. One coin, to those who work against me. That's how I put it right.
accepted: Here. Any of them that free slaves. Say the debt is paid. Say nothing else. Come back and tell me it was taken.
Take it. One of the ninjas who work against us, they come and go. Put it in a hand and say paid in full.
It is only a coin. It is the only one I can part with without anyone noticing. Say paid in full, and bring me word.
Here. If anyone asks, you found it. Come back after, and say they took it.

say: Put your hand down. What's in it? A coin? Why would a coin worry me?
You're hiding something in your fist. Either it's a knife or it's a coin.
That coin is bent. Someone made it so on purpose. Where did you get it?
Hold it up where I can see it. Huh.
reply: A man who sells slaves sent it. He says the debt is paid in full.
A slaver. He wants it to reach you. Paid in full, he said.
From someone in the trade. He said you would know what it means.
I was asked to bring it. The debt is paid, he said.
after: A slaver paying. That is a first. We will take it, because the coin is not his fault. Tell him it was received. Not forgiven.
Paid in full? It never is. But we will put it where it does good. Tell him that.
Do not expect thanks. Expect it to be used. Tell the one who gave it that it was taken.
Huh. Then he has a conscience. Or a rope in his dreams. Either way, take word back. Taken. Nothing more.

say: Taken. Not forgiven, I'd guess. Good.
They took it? Then it is settled. I will not say it is a weight off. It is a weight shifted. Take these.
Received. I thought they would spit on it. Take what I owe you.
Done, then. Don't tell anyone I was ever decent.
I'm obliged. A little. Keep the cats and keep quiet.
I have a note for my brother. He took up with a rough crowd. Mongrel, last I heard. I can't go. Would you put it in someone's hand there?
Do you travel by the Mongrel places? A note. Sealed. For a man whose name I won't say aloud.
I have a sealed note and a brother I haven't seen in years. People like him end up with people like the Mongrel. Would you?
Please. I didn't write it well. It only needs to get to him. Anywhere among the Mongrel will do to start.
accepted: Here. No name. They will pass it among themselves, or they will not. Say it is from family. Come back and tell me.
Take it. It is sealed with tallow. Do not open it. Put it in a Mongrel hand and say it is from home. Then tell me.
Thank you. Say it is from the one who stayed. They will understand. Come back to me after.
Here. If they ask, I am nobody. Just say home. Bring word after.

say: What's that? You're holding it like it might go off.
You carry a note. We don't get notes. We get knives and rumours. Who from?
A sealed thing. Give it here if it's for one of us, or put it away.
Is that tallow on it? Who still seals notes with tallow? Who sent it?
reply: Family, for someone who ended up with you. I do not know his name.
From home. A brother who stayed. It needs to reach his.
A note from someone who misses him.
Sealed. I was told to say it is from home.
after: Home. Hah. Give it here. If it is for one of us it will find him. Tell the sender I said so.
Leave it. We have people who read and people who do not, and the note will find both. Tell the sender it was taken.
A note from home. I will see it goes where it should. That is the best I can say. Go.
Funny. Most notes here are warnings. A letter from home. Hand it over and walk on.

say: They took it. Thank you. I didn't know if anyone would. Here's some coin, and my father's katana. It has hung on my wall for years and I'm no swordsman.
It will reach him, or it won't. But it has left my hands. Take these cats, and the blade by the door.
You put it in the right hands? I hope so. I'll stop wondering now. Here, my father's old katana, and what I saved.
Thank you. I was afraid of that last step. Take the cats, and this katana. It was his, and he would not have wanted it rusting.
Another woman told me she gave a stranger something to carry. If that was you, do not stop now.
I will not ask what you carry or who for. I will only say, whoever it is, keep it dry and keep walking.
Someone spoke to me of a stranger and a cord. If it is you, I am glad. Go on quietly.
I hear a traveller has a small thing from one of us. Do not show it to any robe.
Another of us said a stranger took a cord out. She would not say more. Was it you?
Somebody carried a cord out of here. I heard it from three mouths and I believe none of them. Was it you?
They say a cord got past the gates. I was not asked and I did not look. Thank you, if it was you.
A stranger took something small out for one of us. We don't speak of it.
Cord with knots, you carried? Word reached us. Somebody inside is still counting.
Some of us heard about a cord from inside the Nation. We've been quiet about it, the way you're quiet about good news.
I heard a cord came out of the Holy Nation. I'd like to know whose hand tied it.
The cord that came out was kept. I did not see it. Nobody saw it.
Priests say a knot in a cord is a debt. The women say it is a name. I say it is none of my business.
My wife ties knots in her thread when she thinks I'm not looking.
A pilgrim was searched at a gate for letters. They found a cord and let her go. I would not know why.
I heard a woman can hide a great deal in a sleeve. They say it as a warning.
Things get out of the Holy Nation if you wait. Words, mostly. Once in a while a bit of string.
We get messages from inside, now and then. They're never signed.
A woman in the Nation once sent word by a beggar. We never found the beggar.
People think nobody inside the walls is still thinking. They are wrong, and I have the proof, though not on me.
They say the Holy Nation keeps its women quiet. Quiet isn't the same as empty.
I knew a Holy Nation woman once. She said less than anyone and remembered more.
Out of the Nation, you can carry words, goods or nothing at all. The nothing is the most dangerous.
Never ask a Holy Nation woman where she's going. She will tell you the truth, and it will be worse than a lie.
The Inquisitors have been asking after cords and knots. They will not say why.
A priest looked at a sleeve for a long time today. I don't know what he thought he saw.
I hear someone is asking questions near the women. No one answers them, and that is an answer too.
There was a search, and nothing was found, and everyone looked pleased about it. I do not trust that.
Somebody brought us a cord from inside the Nation. We haven't stopped talking about it.
A knotted cord reached us from inside. Each knot is a person. We read them all.
Whoever carried that cord out, we owe them. We just don't know how to say it.
We kept the cord. We didn't keep the carrier's name. We didn't need it.
Someone spoke of a ronin and a strip of hide. If you're the one carrying it, don't stop.
You carry the count? Good. Don't lose it. It's the only thing I have asked anyone for.
I heard a ronin gave a stranger his marks. I'd like to be the stranger, and I'm not.
The days aren't heavy. They're only many. Take them to the hive.
A ronin I know said he gave his days to a traveller and the hive kept them. He's quieter since. It's a good quiet.
I heard the hive kept someone's count. It is not much. It is more than most of us get.
A stranger took a ronin's marks to the hive. The ronin doesn't say it, but he's lighter.
Another of us sent his count to the hive. They kept it. I'm thinking about doing the same.
Someone brought a count to one of us. It was kept. I don't know why that matters, but it's spoken of.
A strip with cuts came from outside. The hive holds it. The hive doesn't say more.
We were given the days of one who left. We hold them. It is enough.
A traveller came with marks. We do not forget marks.
Ronin cut marks in things. Hide, wood, their own arms, some of them. I don't ask which days they're counting.
I knew a ronin who said it was too quiet out here. I told him it wasn't, with the raptors about.
Some hive princes lose the hive and keep the habits.
A ronin doesn't sleep like we do. I have watched. He lies down and listens for something.
Some of the lost ones count. We don't know what they count.
The hive hears many things. It doesn't always hear the lost ones.
A lost one passed our way. He didn't stop. He looked like he was listening.
We do not speak of those who left. We notice them.
Hive ronin are strange company. Polite, careful, and never quite here.
I heard a ronin counting once, under his breath, over and over. It was the same number.
Never share a fire with a ronin unless you can stand silence. They give a lot of it.
A ronin told me he doesn't miss the hive. He said it three times.
Somebody carried a notched strip of hide to a hiver and the hiver took it without a fuss.
A ronin gave away his days and a hiver kept them. I'd like to have seen it.
I hear a stranger took a ronin's marks to the hive. People in my line of work don't do that sort of thing for free.
A ronin walked away lighter this week. I saw it.
An outsider brought a count to one of us.
A drone took marks from a stranger and did not ask for coin. We noticed.
We hold the days of one who left.
The hive keeps what it's given. It was given a count.
You carry a hide for me. Don't stop. Don't ask.
A Shek of the Kingdom, with his horns. Not one who has left.
Another told me of a /FLATSKIN/ with a hide. If that is you, you are slow.
The hide isn't heavy. It isn't meant to be. Put it where it belongs.
Another Shek told me a /FLATSKIN/ carried a hide for him. I said nothing then.
I heard a hide was returned to the Kingdom by a stranger. It isn't for me to ask by whom.
A debt was paid in leather. I don't know whose. I'm glad it wasn't mine.
Someone carried a thing for a Shek who can't go home. That isn't nothing.
A /FLATSKIN/ brought leather to the Kingdom for one who is not here. Speak of it to no one.
Something was returned. I didn't see by whom. The mark on it was scraped.
We got a hide from outside. We kept it. We say nothing of who.
A stranger walked in with a debt that was not his. He paid it. That is rare.
There are Shek who walk outside the Kingdom. We do not name them.
A Shek leaves the Kingdom and the Kingdom does not say a word. That is how you know.
Some who left will come home. Some won't. Some won't be asked.
Hrm. Outside the Kingdom a Shek is only a tall /FLATSKIN/ with horns. He knows it.
Shek do not forget. If one owes the Kingdom, he owes it until he dies. I would not carry his debt.
Shek mercenaries say they have no home, and then they look at the horizon the way they look at it.
A Shek will hold a grudge for longer than you'll live. A Shek will also hold a promise.
I knew a Shek who sold his sword to anyone but wouldn't sell his hide.
Never touch a Shek's leather. They know when it has been touched.
The Shek keep marks on things. I don't know what they mean.
I saw a Shek scrape a mark off a strip of hide for most of a night. He didn't look up.
Shek don't apologise. They sometimes leave a thing where you'll find it.
Something was returned to the Kingdom by a /FLATSKIN/'s hand. No one will say what. Everyone is quiet about it.
A strip of hide came back. The one who sent it isn't named.
A debt was paid by proxy. A Shek would have preferred to pay it himself.
We had a visitor with a hide. He left. We did not ask his name.
A traveller put a strip of hide in a Shek's hand and walked away whole. The Shek still talk about the manners.
I hear someone carried something to the Kingdom for a Shek who can't. That's a nasty errand and he did it.
A /FLATSKIN/ returned leather to the Kingdom. They didn't kill him.
Somebody took a debt to the Shek for a stranger. They say it was taken without a word. That's good with the Shek.
You have my page? Don't use it to light a fire. Find a skeleton and have it read.
Another hunter said a stranger has a page to read. If that's you, don't dawdle.
Page, skeleton, words. Then me. That's all of the job.
I hope you aren't a thief with a page. I know where to find thieves.
A page went to a skeleton. I heard about it. Don't tell me what was written.
Another hunter said a stranger took a page off for reading. I wondered who it was.
I heard the page was read. I hear it was nothing. I hear that a lot.
A traveller did a job for a hunter and came back whole. That's more than usual.
You read pages. I have a drawer full of them. Nobody asks what they say. They only ask if they're worth anything.
A page came to us not long ago, and left again. I do not know what became of it.
We read what we're given. It's our function. It's sometimes not enough.
A stranger brought written material once. We read it. We said nothing else. That seems to be the rule.
Skeletons read anything you hand them, I hear.
A Tech Hunter paid a man to carry a page to a skeleton once. Said he wouldn't touch it himself. He wasn't joking, I think.
Old paper from the ruins is more trouble than it's worth. Nobody can read it and nobody wants to be seen with it.
I never trusted a page that was written by someone who is dead. They write as if they will be read.
A page off a dead man is still a page.
The ruins give up paper more easily than coin. Paper is worse.
You find a lot of writing in the old places. Most of it's just lists.
I do not read old script. I know a few who do.
We read and aren't thanked for it. That isn't a complaint.
Paper does not last. We last.
We were given a page once. It was almost nothing.
Writing is a way to be found. Most of it isn't found.
A page was read to a stranger and the stranger left.
A traveller took a reading and left. That is the usual pattern.
We read for a stranger recently. No payment.
A page now belongs to us. It was not stolen. It was left.
I hear someone found a use for a dead man's page. I'd like it to have been me.
A page changed hands and nobody was killed. That is odd.
Somebody did a hunter's errand and didn't ask for double. I'd like to know them.
A hunter got his reading and it cost him only a fair price.
You have my coin. Don't spend it. It would be funny, and then it wouldn't.
Another trader said you carry a coin for someone. I didn't hear it from me.
Carry it on, and say nothing. It's the only way this works.
I did not ask for sympathy. Only a pair of legs.
Another dealer said a coin went out to the other side. It isn't talked about.
I heard a slaver paid a debt he didn't have to. It's bad for business to be known for that.
Somebody carried a coin for one of us. I never heard it.
The trade has its own conscience, and it's very small. Someone fed it. Good.
A bent coin came to me from a slaver. I don't know what to make of it.
A coin reached us. Someone sold people for the money before it, and then wished he hadn't.
We got a coin from the trade. We used it for something.
A trader's conscience arrived by hand. We aren't sure what to do with those.
I knew a slaver who paid a man's way home and called it a loss on the books.
Everyone in this trade has a column they don't look at.
The trade doesn't forgive. The trade only forgets, for a price.
You can hear a man come to hate his work. It sounds like very careful accounting.
They say the anti-slaver ninjas take coin from anyone who doesn't ask for anything back.
Coins turn up at the ninjas from strange hands. They don't ask whose.
I don't mind who gives, so long as they don't want thanks. Thanks cost more than coin.
Money is money. It doesn't know where it has been.
Slavers feel nothing, so I hear. The ones I knew felt plenty. They billed it elsewhere.
A slaver once gave me bread. I took it. I didn't thank him. I didn't forget it either.
A coin can be a bribe, a payment or an apology. You can only tell by what the hand does after.
People are bought and sold in this world, and the people doing it still go home to supper.
Somebody carried coin out of a slave shop to the other side. Nobody says whose. The books are quiet on it.
One of us paid a debt in the wrong direction. I admire it. I won't be copying it.
I hear a coin went missing and then turned up in the right place. Don't look for the thief.
The trade lost one coin and gained a clean conscience for a dealer.
A slaver's coin reached us. It was bent. I don't know what to make of it.
They say a trader sent us money from his own pocket. It isn't much. It's something.
We have coin from the trade now and we're using it against the trade.
A bent coin, a stranger, a message. Not many messages come our way that don't mean a fight.
You have the note? Don't open it. Please. It isn't much, but it's mine.
Someone told me a traveller was carrying a note for family. I hope that's you.
If you haven't gone yet, I understand. If you've lost it, tell me.
Say it is from home. Nothing else is needed.
Someone said a note went to the Mongrel for one of us. I hope it was read.
A stranger carried a letter out for a neighbour. We do not talk of it.
I hear a note was delivered. I don't know what it said. I hope it said sorry.
Somebody got a note through to a brother. It's good to hear of anything getting through.
A note came in from outside. A man read it and sat down. I won't say who.
There was a note from home. It was handled with more care than anything we own.
A sealed note came, and someone kept it.
We got a letter by a stranger. We don't get many. We aren't good with them.
The Mongrel will have anyone, they say, so long as you can fight or fool somebody.
Half the families in the Cities have someone they don't speak of. Gone to the bandits, gone to the sand. You learn to stop looking up the road.
I knew a man who wrote to his brother every year. He never got an answer.
A letter is the most dangerous thing you can carry. It can make a person turn around.
A note came in once, years back. A man read it twice and left in the night.
Everyone here left someone. We don't talk of it.
A message from home is a bad omen or a good one. You can't tell until you read it.
I once burned a letter unread. I think about it more than I should.
I had a cousin who went to the Mongrel. We didn't write. I think we should have.
